- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or erratic, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days show high volatility or mean-reversion signals, reduce forecast magnitude by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ days of 0.67–1.00), model tends to overforecast; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to offset.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves if sentiment is weak or recent price is declining; prefer conservative, lagged trend alignment.
